title: As Twilight's Gradual Veil Is Spread
description: As Twilight's Gradual Veil Is Spread in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Edward Smith wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 551 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Changes of Nature Types of Immortality”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: As twi-light's grad-ual veil is spread A-cross th'e-ve-ning sky; So man's bright hours de-cline in shade, And mor-tal com-forts die.

lines: As twilight's gradual veil is spread
So man's bright hours decline in shade,
The bloom of spring, the summer rose,
Nor youth, nor age, nor wisdom knows
But morning dawns and spring revives,
When this vain scene no longer charms,
He sinks into a Father's arms,

licence: Public domain: James Edward Smith died in 1828.
credits: Words by James Edward Smith (1759–1828), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
